rationale: Three correctness angles (line-by-line, removed-behavior, cross-file callers) and cleanup/conventions angles ran. No correctness bugs found. One PLAUSIBLE finding (empty-string fileName produces degraded aria-label) is a pre-existing type-system gap not introduced by this diff — uploadedFiles: string[] has never guarded empty strings, and File.name (the primary call site) is non-empty per browser spec. One cleanup finding (cursor-pointer redundant on button) is below blocking threshold. focus-visible:ring-border-accent is confirmed as the project-wide convention (5+ components). No blocking findings.

findings.summary: aria-label degrades to 'Remove file ' if fileName is an empty string
findings.failure_scenario: uploadedFiles: string[] permits empty strings at the type level; no guard exists at FileListItem, FileList, or FilesDropzone. If the backend returns '' in uploaded_files, the button gets aria-label 'Remove file ' — a screen-reader-announced label with no file context. Pre-existing gap, not introduced by this diff. File.name (primary call site) is non-empty per browser spec, so risk is low in practice.

findings.summary: cursor-pointer is redundant on a <button> element
findings.failure_scenario: Browsers apply pointer cursor to <button> by default; Tailwind preflight does not remove it. Dead utility class with no visual effect. Below blocking threshold — consistent with existing patterns in the codebase.
